doc.title: Frank Capp interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Working with Marty Paich, other soloists, and The Red Skelton Show
summary: Asked about Art Pepper and Stan Getz, Capp talks of Marty Paich, Benny Carter and Ray Brown, and twelve years on the live Red Skelton Show with David Rose.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: What about some of the, you’ve worked with some great soloists too — Art Pepper, and Stan Getz.
Art Pepper, Stan Getz, I worked with Marty Paich. In fact, did you know Marty Paich, the pianist?
I know of him. I never met him.

He was a great arranger. Great arranger and great piano player too. And I did a lot of work with him. Do you know I can’t remember, I mean there’s so many. I mean you name ‘em, I probably worked with them. Benny Carter, Ray Brown. I did twelve years on The Red Skelton Show when, fellows who remember variety television, I did that with David Rose.
Yeah, that was a live show.
